observations: Rotary hammer drill lying on a dusty ground surface.
Label on the tool body clearly shows 'Ramset' brand and 'DD560' model.
The label also identifies the tool as a 'ROTARY HAMMER'.
The tool is orange and black with a side handle and a rear D-handle.
A black power cord is visible, coiled at the bottom right.
The exterior shows signs of use, including dust and minor scuffs.

claims.claim: for drilling, punch, chisel and breaking
claims.evidence: photo 0 label identifies it as a rotary hammer, which performs these functions

risks.proof: Video of the tool powered on and hammering into concrete.

risks.risk: Worn or damaged chuck (bit holder) failing to secure bits
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the chuck and video of a bit being locked in.

risks.risk: Mode selector switch is jammed or non-functional
risks.proof: Video showing the selector switch being moved through all settings.

proof_requests: Video of the tool running and demonstrating the hammering action.
Close-up photo of the chuck (bit entry point).
Photo of the full rating plate to confirm voltage (e.g., 110v vs 220v).
response.reason: The item is clearly identified by brand and model from the photo. It will be priced as non-functional due to the lack of proof that the motor or hammering mechanism works.
